core_obligations: Left exactness (proof line 1461): the inclusion of abelian sheaves into abelian presheaves preserves kernels, hence is left exact.
Describe the derived functors (proof lines 1462-1464): choosing an injective resolution F -> I^bullet, the functor R^p i is by definition the p-th cohomology presheaf of the complex I^bullet.

Identify the sections (proof lines 1464-1471): over an object U the sections of R^p i(F) are ker(I^n(U) -> I^{n+1}(U)) / im(I^{n-1}(U) -> I^n(U)), which is the definition of H^p(U, F), giving the stated description of R^p i as the cohomology presheaf U -> H^p(U, F).
proof_roadmap: Note that the inclusion of abelian sheaves into presheaves is left exact.
Compute the right derived functors from an injective resolution.
Over an object U the resulting presheaf is kernel modulo image of the section complex.
That is H^p(U, F), so the derived functors form the cohomology presheaf.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the right derived functors of the inclusion of abelian sheaves into abelian presheaves with the cohomology presheaves U -> H^p(U, F) (statement lines 1447-1458). The proof is a definitional computation: left exactness is immediate, and after choosing an injective resolution in Ab(C) the derived functors are the cohomology presheaves of the resolution complex, whose sections over U are kernel modulo image of the section complex, which is precisely the definition of H^p(U, F) (proof lines 1461-1471). The claim is H2: one definition unfolded carefully, with no additional construction.
